keys.note: unset = the DS is its own domain
<profile-id>=<digest>[,...]; id [A-Za-z0-9._-]{1,63}; a record whose profile id is not pinned or whose digest differs from its pin is rejected

connector_client.endpoint_rule: endpoint.server == registry.host; endpoint.port == registry.tcp_port when both set; trailing '/' is ignored on every path; without endpoint.ds_path: endpoint.export_path == registry.export_path; with endpoint.ds_path: ds_path == registry.export_path and export_path == ds_path or a component-wise ancestor of it; '/' is never a parent; every path is canonical: no empty, '.' or '..' component
connector_client.rebind_rule: a strictly higher binding_generation re-pins and clears the verdict of the old binding: the DS is neutral until the first VALID record of the new binding; any other change is BINDING_MISMATCH
connector_client.reachable_rule: an accepted batch within 3 x ds_connector_poll_ms; recomputed on every failure kind (CONNECT, TIMEOUT, HTTP, UNAVAILABLE, DROP) and mirrored by pnfs_mds_connector_reachable
connector_client.contract_version_rule: <major>.<rest>: digits, no leading zero, a '.' must follow the major; the major equals ds_connector_expected_contract_major
connector_client.sequence_rule: per (instance, epoch): equal = the same snapshot re-served (accepted, rows re-timed); lower = REPLAY (batch dropped); a new runtime_epoch resets every line and pin but keeps the verdicts; at most 64 instance lines, a batch needing more is refused
connector_client.profile_rule: per record: with pins set, profile.id must be pinned and its digest equal the pin; one id with two digests, or more than 8 ids, drops the batch; checked on every batch, not part of the per-DS pin (a connector profile reload is not a rebind)
connector_client.duplicate_rule: a ds_id present more than once in a batch has no trusted record and pins nothing
connector_client.string_rule: standard JSON escapes decoded, \uXXXX with surrogate pairs; lone surrogates and \u0000 are shape errors
connector_client.http_client: Unix socket, Content-Length framing only (Transfer-Encoding is refused), body <= 4 MiB, EOF before Content-Length = TIMEOUT-class failure, MSG_NOSIGNAL
connector_client.unobserved_incarnation_rule: target_incarnation null is legal on a quality UNKNOWN record and on a VALID deny (the connector's evidence-less denies, SHARE_ABSENT and IDENTITY_MISMATCH): the tuple is compared without the incarnation, the pin is neither created nor changed (a higher generation clears it); an UNKNOWN record is no new data; a VALID allow with a null incarnation is a shape error
connector_client.retention_rule: a VALID verdict stays in force for remaining_ttl_ms without a new one (the connector sets it: critical_hold_ms for a critical verdict, allowed=false, verdict_hold_ms for any other, counted from the observation, or from the fetch for a deny that carries no evidence time such as SHARE_ABSENT or IDENTITY_MISMATCH); a newer VALID record replaces it at once; UNKNOWN, rejected and dropped records never replace it; a FAILED snapshot carries only VERDICT_RETAINED records; a rebind clears it and a runtime_epoch change keeps it; no verdict in force = neutral (1 000 000 ppm on the base weight of the operator's capacity domain: its placement_domain_weight.<domain> under placement_allow_manual_base_weights, else the fill level; the DS state, capacity and alias gates still apply)

verify_exit.0: same effective mode, generation and build on every MDS and no error reported; smart on an MDS with verdict retention: an unreachable connector and coverage partial or none are warnings (the cluster places neutrally, it does not steer)
verify_exit.1: any difference, a desired mode not yet effective, connector_config_valid=0, a connector config digest or profile map that differs between MDS, an unreadable (CONNECTOR_PROFILES_INVALID) or, in smart, absent (CONNECTOR_PROFILES_MISSING) profile pin row; in smart an MDS that admits no DS (NO_ELIGIBLE_DS: registered_ds > 0, eligible_ds = 0) and, against an MDS that predates verdict retention (no retained_ds/neutral_ds in its readiness row), an unreachable connector or coverage none (COVERAGE_NONE); with --require-full-coverage also partial, none or retained coverage
verify_exit.2: an MDS could not be read
